title: Gravitational-wave mergers
summary: Pairs of black holes and neutron stars that spiralled together and merged, heard by LIGO, Virgo and KAGRA.

concepts.label: Compact binary coalescence
concepts.description: The merger of two black holes or neutron stars, detected by its gravitational waves.

children.label: Source-frame mass
children.description: Each object's mass in solar masses, corrected for redshift; median of the posterior.

children.label: Effective spin
children.description: χ_eff: the mass-weighted spin along the orbital axis, −1 to 1.

children.label: Luminosity distance
children.description: Distance in megaparsecs inferred from the signal's amplitude.

children.label: Radiated energy
children.description: Total minus final mass: what left as gravitational waves.

children.label: Black hole
children.description: A compact object above about 3 solar masses here.

children.label: Neutron star
children.description: A compact object below about 3 solar masses here.

concepts.label: Observing run
concepts.description: A period the detectors took science data (O1–O4).
